architect.reply:
Yes
The architectural design of the verification loop is sound, minimal, and directly enforceable. Capturing the unpiped exit code and raw output to a file removes silent failure modes caused by upstream pipe masks. Verifying branch alignment via explicit fetch and commit confirmation via local log inspection eliminates false positives without introducing heavy tooling overhead. The trial scope of three cards and the counter-metric bounding execution time to under one minute per push ensure the rule remains lightweight and operationally sustainable.

CITE: every push writes its whole output and its own exit code to a file
